posts.cooked:
This is an interaction I found last week: If damage dealt by incidental contract is redirected the new target may be dealt the 1 additional energy damage rather than the original target. So in a 5 hero game Wrong Time and Place can turn Incidental Contact into 12 separate attacks against the villain. Add Twist the Either and KNYFE’s damage boosts and this can become 48 damage to the villain at the cost of only 5 unlucky tokens. In the process of discovering this I dropped Ambuscade from full HP to incapped in a single turn.

Another interaction I discovered a while ago but enjoy putting to use is that Hippocractic Oath can heal for 1 extra point if you target The Idealist (or Mainstay/Writhe if thier signatures aren’t out) with Medico’s initial attack due to Sentinels Nemesis Bonus.

Lastly, team up Santa Guise and Freedom 6 Tempest. Tempest can target his presents with his base power (though Guise may not appreciate you returning his gifts).

Silver Lining may or may not stop the chain.

If you hit the a target first and then start the friendly fire chain when Silver Lining triggers you’ll still have the second hit of your original attack to resolve… starting the chain up a second time (if you have a second silver lining that one will break the chain.

If you hit 2 targets first and choose not to trigger friendly fire off the first hit, then Silver Lining will break the chain.

Only powers that directly deal damage or destroy targets can earn Living Weapon.  Playing a card that deals damage does not earn it.  Triggering an effect that deals damage does not earn it.  Dealing damage and then finishing them off with Deathcaller or Flawless Execution does not earn it.  The power must be the direct cause of the destruction by a damage or destroy effect written into the power.

Similarly, damage written in the power is the only damage boosted by it, just like with Hasty Augmentation.

I don’t know if “Unexpected combinations” is the right place for this, but what the heck.

The “Randomize” button gave me a fun setup that had an unusual conclusion, which I’ll call Spam Musubi.

Kaargra Warfang vs DW Expat, Setting Sun Ra, F5 Legacy, Akash SotV, and La Comodora in the Temple of Zhu Long. (I was initially concerned about Akash giving the Bloodsworn more targets to destroy, but it didn’t matter)

It went something like this:

  • I think Kaargra played both of her Bloodsworn Judgements
  • Expat plays Assault Rifle; seeing Shock Rounds also in her hand, she uses Aim to set up next round.
  • Ra probably played his Staff, then Blazed.
  • Legacy played something (I don’t think he had Inspiring Presence, though that would have been fun), then let Ra play Imbued Fire
  • Akash did something, I don’t remember.
  • LaC played Paradoja Figurehead and sent it to Expat
  • The environment gave me a Shinobi Assassin
  • Kaargra played a couple of victims for me.
  • Expat played Shock Rounds, then Fired Assault Rifle at her victims. With Aim, Fire, and Pardoja, that was 5 damage from the Assault Rifle, and 4 from Shock Rounds. More if I had Inspiring Presence.

I realized that the gladiators weren’t going to survive the round, which meant that Kaargra was going to flip. But seeing the amount of favor I’d racked up, I realized that had a chance if I could repeatedly abuse that assassin enough. So I put it on top of Expat’s deck. Then Ra wiped the board, and I put the assassin on Ra’s deck. Repeat with help from Thrashing Brambles and Temporal Rigging, and I just made it, with favor 20-2, before the environment got a second turn.

In some fighting games, spamming the same cheap move over and over will get you booed. Apparently these fans LOVED seeing that poor ninja get brutally killed over and over. I’m going to call him Kenny from now on.

I’ve replayed the scenario numerous times, and have had a lot of fun with it. Kaargra has only managed to win once (darn Fickle Fans). Some more fun:

  • Resurrection Ritual which keeps “Get Back In There!” from returning gladiators to play
  • Take Down and As the Earth Turns keep Kaargra from playing, and LaC’s power lets her return those cards to their decks.
